reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short at around 5 feet 2 inches is a widespread historical misconception. At his autopsy, Napoleon was recorded as measuring 5 feet 2 inches in pre-metric French units (*pieds du roi*), which corresponds to approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (around 168–169 cm) in modern imperial units. For French men in the early 19th century, the average height was around 5 feet 4 to 5 feet 5 inches, meaning Napoleon was of average or slightly above-average stature for his time. The myth of his shortness was popularized by English unit translation errors and British wartime propaganda (such as caricatures by James Gillray).
